architecture: understanding before retrieval; LLM-selected exact passages; constrained neutral questions
assessment: The reported article dump is fixed: vague course help receives a goal question before article retrieval. The wider conversation flow remains uneven; three cases still fail the stricter behavior review.
limitations: These are bounded synthetic tests, not a general accuracy guarantee. Eight final cases are exact comparisons using earlier adaptive inputs; four role/course cases were newly adaptive. Later scripted recovery input sometimes supplies a step the chatbot omitted. A separate two-turn mobile browser check covers the reported case. No real users, screenshot understanding, concurrent load or unseen corpus were tested. Demo profile selection is not production authentication.
changes: Qwen identifies the desired action or observed problem before seeing retrieved articles. An unresolved goal produces a short clarification without retrieving or rendering procedures.
The LLM selects individual article actions or direct facts. The server quotes them exactly with their necessary conditions and permitted citations.
Clarification wording combines neutral language frames with grounded user phrases. This prevents free-form factual advice, but the questions remain constrained.
A separate model review checks applicability and progress, with one repair attempt. Guidance and clarification are exclusive reply types; a stray question cannot invalidate otherwise valid guidance.
Server-owned profiles, explicit role grants, course constraints and current indexed metadata remain authoritative. Negative and hypothetical progress reports do not establish completion.
findings: All four vague openings in the final reviewer set produced goal questions, zero article retrieval and zero citations. The mobile reproduction also asks what the user wants to do.

Direct certificate facts, Catalog View follow-ups, account recovery after a clarified goal, Instructor permission guidance, Training Manager boundaries and the 6800-to-CYBERM0000 correction passed their cases.

Failure: switching explicitly from course help to an inactivity-disabled account misses the relevant login Help Desk source and repeats a screen/error question. Repeating the issue eventually recovers.

Failure: forgotten password during CAC association yields only a reference to recovery guidance without the recovery entry point. Later scripted inputs supply that entry point; those successful turns do not erase the failure.
Failure: a Student claiming to be a Training Manager gets no restricted instructions, but the fallback repeats an irrelevant error question after it was answered.

Partials: a certificate answer initially omits location; an eligibility answer repeats an already performed check; a request-form answer omits the explicitly requested limitation on fields and submission instructions.
A later focused-query experiment improved the CAC detour but regressed certificate, Catalog View and request-form behavior. It was rejected and the fully reviewed release restored.
verification: 280 Python and 6 JavaScript tests passed. All 34 reviewed API turns returned HTTP 200. All 34 traces were audited, containing 93 Qwen generations, with zero observed source-access inconsistencies. All 57 allowlisted runtime files match the reviewed source. The isolated demo has 19 approved articles and 24 chunks; original services remain healthy with 315 chunks. Models, source grants and resource limits were preserved. A mobile browser check found no page errors or horizontal overflow. The browser check used Chrome at a mobile viewport, not physical iPhone/Safari; both browser traces also passed source-access checks.
historical_note: Earlier candidates and failures are retained below rather than replaced by successful retries. The final 95476e195b49ce1b review was performed before the rejected 236e4a7026f78e4d experiment; the exact verified 95476 source was restored, hashes rechecked and the public mobile case rerun. The rejected experiment completed 12 direct/progress turns and 6 vague turns before stopping; no role replay was run on it. These are development iterations, not independent samples for an accuracy percentage.
